title: Chapter 219: Like the Real Thing
html:
“Mr. Han, are you certain the right scenario is less frightening?” Xiao Du clung to the door handle, suddenly longing for Tian Teng Medical School and the safety of his steel box.

“Why are you panicking? That Chen fellow said the Third Sick Hall is unfinished. How frightening can an incomplete scenario be?” Han Qiuming recovered first and seized Guo Miao’s arm. “Old Guo, we’ll lead.”

“What has it got to do with me?” Guo Miao shook him off. “Didn’t you say you’re going to go alone?”

“I’m worried you’ll run halfway through.” Han Qiuming’s expression darkened, hidden by the gloom. “Fine. I’ll lead. Stay close and don’t fall behind.”

Han Qiuming pushed the door wide, showering rust onto the floor. They entered beneath an indescribable stench. Discarded pills and patient files littered the corridor. Han Qiuming advanced alone, but every sight loosened another thread of his confidence.

Madness and despair covered the walls, making every reader’s skin crawl. No sane mind could have conceived those words. Deeper inside, the bloody messages multiplied, overlapping without a single repetition.

“How did he invent all of this? Is he actually insane?” Han Qiuming crouched and pulled back one mattress, revealing a crude doll made from pillows and sheets. Despite its rough construction, he could not look away.

“So even this can become a Haunted House prop? I’ve learned something today.” He knew Chen Ge had probably painted the doll’s face, yet it still unsettled him deeply.

“Look at this!” Su Luoluo stood outside the first patient room, pointing at a doorknob streaked with blood and gouged by fingernails.

She compared the marks with her fingers. “They look genuine, not carved with tools.”

“You think the designer gouged the door with his own hands?” Han Qiuming covered the doll again. “Don’t touch anything. You may trigger a mechanism. Pay particular attention to the mattresses; actors may be hiding inside.”

He moved on, but the others remained behind while Ye Xiaoxin entered the room alone. Wooden slats covered the windows, with solid concrete visible beyond them. The sealed space felt less like a hospital room than a prison cell.

Ye Xiaoxin ran a finger along the bedframe and found gouges in its side. “Help me lift this.”

“We have only twenty minutes. Can you move faster and ignore the irrelevant details?” Han Qiuming waited alone outside while Xiao Du and Song An helped Ye Xiaoxin. What they found beneath the bed surprised them all.

A long, dark-red gouge scored the wood, broken fingernails embedded in its grooves—a record of unbearable pain.

“Fake blood fades when it dries. This dark-red stain…” Song An recoiled and whispered to Ye Xiaoxin, “It looks human.”

“Are you certain it isn’t artificial?” Ye Xiaoxin bent close and sniffed the groove. “There’s no smell.”

Her nerve startled Song An. He laughed awkwardly. “It may be pig or cow blood. Some Haunted Houses use animal blood for authenticity.”

“Bloodstained props are common, especially in an independent attraction like Boss Chen’s. He probably bought much of this from abandoned hospitals.” Guo Miao sounded experienced. “Either way, remain cautious. The blood means something terrible happened in this hospital.”

Ye Xiaoxin nodded. “What about the bloody scratches on the doorknob? Was that taken from the hospital too?”

Guo Miao was stumped.

“You can’t explain it either.” Ye Xiaoxin opened her notebook. “Most Haunted Houses concentrate detail around specific scares. Here, every detail feels authentic, as though the owner is obsessive.”

“I noticed something worse.” Su Luoluo looked at the ceiling, where bloody sentences seemed to shift before her eyes. “Every message uses different handwriting. They weren’t written by one person.”

“Different handwriting?” Guo Miao examined the walls and grew paler. “You’re right. How did Boss Chen create all this?”

Han Qiuming returned when he realized no one had followed. Leaning against the doorway, he boasted, “Didn’t he say this Haunted House has operated for years? Give me five years, and I’ll build something better.”

“Would you spend five years on one scenario?” Guo Miao’s annoyance grew. His careful arrangements had been ruined by Han Qiuming. “Boss Chen probably told the truth. This is his hardest scenario. We should find the recorder and leave.”

Unease had followed him from the moment they entered, intensifying with every detail: bloody scratches on the doorknob, gouges in the bedframe, messages across walls and ceiling. Buried memories awakened, carrying him back to the hospital where Xu Zhenzhen had died.

“Old Guo, I never knew you were such a coward. I admit the attention to detail is impressive, but that proves only his talent for imitation.” Han Qiuming glanced covertly at Ye Xiaoxin and adjusted his glasses. “A major overseas Haunted House I visited used props from an actual prison. Compared with that, this is barely acceptable.”

“You’ll regret that overconfidence soon enough.”

“I’m only telling the truth.” Han Qiuming waved them onward. “We have sixteen minutes left. Move.”

The group continued, leaving Xiao Du alone near the entrance. As he stared at the writing, his pulse accelerated. The scattered letters seemed to shift and assemble into a single word.

Death.

“This place is cursed. I’ll wait by the door.”

He stepped outside and looked toward Mu Yang High School. The mannequins that had stood at the corridor’s far end were now disturbingly close.

“What’s going on?”

Xiao Du stumbled backward. Unable to remain alone, he hurried after the group.

After he left, a mannequin with a name tag pinned to its lapel silently adjusted its head.
